## Verdict
needs-revision

## Concerns
- claim-2 is not fully standalone: the proof defines an abstract interval module \(J_{r,q;i,j}\) but never explicitly proves or invokes
  \[
  J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}
  =\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda
  \]
  and its transformed counterpart. Thus the conclusion for the actual \(J_v\) remains conditional, as the draft itself acknowledges.
- The transformed admissibility justification is misstated: \(t'>r'+s'-n'\) follows from \(t>0\), whereas \(t>s-q\) proves \(t'>0\), hence \(t'\ge1\). The conclusions are true, but the implications should be corrected.
- For strict standalone form, \(I_{r,q}\) and the bigrassmannian hypotheses should be stated explicitly. The parameter and family-transposition calculations themselves are correct.

## Unresolved certificates
- [proof-attempt] State \(I_{r,q}\), the full bigrassmannian hypotheses, and explicitly invoke or prove the Schur-basis interval realization of both the original and transformed \(J_v\); then repeat the descent and minimality argument with the corrected admissibility implications.
